solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bleat about leaving leader with others

indicators.note: about here signals that the remaining letters are moved around into a new order
leaving leader means the opening letter of the word bleat is dropped

explanation.surface: A complaint about someone stepping down as head, joined by everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving leader' drops the B of Bleat to leave LEAT, and 'about' rearranges those four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation used in citations means 'and others', standing for the remaining people.

clue.text: Take two photos yet end up with just one

definitions.text: Take two photos yet end up with just one

parts.words: Take two photos yet end up with just one
parts.note: a snap and a shot are both photographs, but joined together they name a single quick photograph

explanation.surface: A photographer shoots twice and somehow ends up with a single picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The two photos are the words SNAP and SHOT; put them side by side and they make one word for one photo.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick informal photograph is called by this compound of two words that each also mean a photograph.

clue.text: Egyptian god's extra-large flag

parts.note: OS, short for outsize, is a clothing label for extra-large
the flag is the yellow iris, a plant of riverbanks

explanation.surface: A huge banner belonging to an Egyptian deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is not a banner but the wild iris plant; OS is the British clothing abbreviation for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the ancient Egyptian deity of the underworld and resurrection, husband of Isis.

clue.text: Though unusually smart he's an annoyance

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters are set out in an unusual new order

explanation.surface: He may be clever, but he's still a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the letters of SMART HE'S AN, apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent unwanted pestering is a form of annoyance, often in a workplace sense.

clue.text: Huge bird caught in area going west

indicators.note: in an across answer, going west means the letters run right to left, backwards

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the tit is a small common garden bird

explanation.surface: A large bird is trapped in a region and heading westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns round everything before it, the bird included, not just the area.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means colossal, from the giant Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: Tenor initially rehearses in the manner of a hum

parts.note: T is a standard abbreviation for tenor in music

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: à la is French for in the manner of

explanation.surface: A tenor starts his practice by humming.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheerful wordless refrain sung or hummed instead of lyrics, a carefree vocal noise.

clue.text: Extraordinary escalation in punishment, ultimately — with this?

definitions.text: Extraordinary escalation in punishment, ultimately — with this?

indicators.note: extraordinary signals that the letters are put into an unusual new arrangement
ultimately means only the final letter of the word punishment is taken

explanation.surface: An outrageous increase in the severity of a penalty, delivered with a whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinary' rearranges ESCALATION IN plus T, the end of 'punishment'. The whole clue also describes the answer: a savage stepping-up of punishment would use this whip.
explanation.definitionFit: The nine-thonged whip was used for flogging in the navy, an extreme form of punishment.

clue.text: On reflection, sketches green turf

indicators.note: on reflection means the word is mirrored, read from right to left

parts.note: to sketch is to draw, so sketches gives draws

explanation.surface: After thinking it over, an artist sketches a grassy lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' looks like 'after thought' but reverses DRAWS.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for an expanse of short grass, a stretch of lawn or turf.

clue.text: Cross over dull person offering little resistance

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix, as in a church's rood screen
matt or mat describes a dull, non-shiny finish

explanation.surface: An angry person brushes past a boring, passive individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry' but is ROOD, reversed by 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lets others walk all over them is called by the name of the mat at the entrance.

clue.text: Name originally used by Prince for conscription

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the word used is taken

explanation.surface: A royal's title was first adopted to recruit soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Summoning citizens for compulsory military service is the drafting process this phrase names.

clue.text: Spanish fighter travelled quickly by damaged road

parts.note: to tear along is to travel at speed, past tense tore

indicators.note: damaged signals that the word road is broken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A Spanish combatant sped along a broken-up road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' signals the rearrangement; 'by' simply joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the bullfighter, especially one on horseback, of Spanish bullrings and Bizet's Carmen.

clue.text: Instruments used when fires, reportedly, circle pub on outskirts of Eccles

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is taken as heard, a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them, so fires gives sacks
a circle is shaped like the letter O
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

indicators.note: outskirts means the outer letters of Eccles, its first and last

explanation.surface: Musicians play while sacked staff gather round a pub near Eccles, a town by Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: SACKS (from 'fires') sounds like SAX, signalled by 'reportedly'; 'outskirts of' gives ES from Eccles.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxophones are reed instruments of the woodwind family, made of brass.

clue.text: Old region developed early. It's above the earth

parts.note: a zone is an area or region

indicators.note: developed signals that the letters of early are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: An ancient territory was settled early, and it lies higher than the land.
explanation.definitionFit: The protective band of a form of oxygen sits in the stratosphere high above the planet's surface.

clue.text: Around the beginning of October Keith met Lois in motion picture

indicators.note: around signals that the letters are moved about into another order
the beginning of means only the opening letter of October is used

explanation.surface: Keith and Lois met in a cinema in early October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' rearranges O (from 'the beginning of October') with KEITH MET LOIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1959 Billy Wilder comedy starring Marilyn Monroe, Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon is a famous film.

clue.text: Gin, say, with dessert can be pleasant but brief

parts.note: in Britain a short is a small strong drink of spirits such as gin
with means together with, so and
in Britain a sweet is a pudding or dessert course

explanation.surface: A gin with pudding makes an agreeable but quick treat.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a 'short' is a spirit served in a small measure, and 'sweet' is the dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something agreeably concise, not dragged out longer than needed.

clue.text: Ground needs time to produce green fodder

parts.note: ground means earth or soil
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Land requires a while before it yields fresh cattle feed.
explanation.definitionFit: This farming term is fresh-cut grass or crops fed to livestock in their stalls.

clue.text: County's housing application, in stone

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a shire is an English county
app is the short form of application

explanation.surface: A county council puts a planning application in for stonework.
explanation.definitionFit: The blue gemstone is a precious stone, a variety of corundum.

clue.text: See 13
Displaying dislike, trick to conceal one course of action

indicators.note: to conceal means to hide something inside, so one part sits within the other

parts.note: an antic is a playful trick or prank
I is the Roman numeral one
a path is a course or route of action

explanation.surface: A prank is used to hide a plan, showing hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal' signals the insertion; 'trick' is the outer piece doing the hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes feeling or showing an aversion, a deep-set hostility.

clue.text: Soon unknown male gets pen name

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so y

explanation.surface: An anonymous man will soon adopt a writing name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an assumed name used to hide identity, a pseudonym under which an author writes.

clue.text: See 13
Yankee Doodle's feather? You could eat it!

definitions.meaning: in the song, Yankee Doodle stuck a feather in his cap and gave it the name of an Italian pasta, slang then for a dandy
the word is also a tube-shaped pasta

explanation.surface: A song's dandy hero has a plume, and it is edible.
explanation.definitionFit: The song calls the feather this, meaning a fop's fashion; it is also an everyday pasta dish.

clue.text: Hot number makes summit

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
eight is a number

explanation.surface: A popular song reaches the top of the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot number' looks like a hit tune but splits into H and EIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak or topmost point of something is its highest level, its apex.

clue.text: Fateful day in Rome that is cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is removed from the Latin phrase

parts.note: id est, Latin for that is, gives the letters

explanation.surface: A doomed day in ancient Rome, so to speak, ends early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the T from ID EST, Latin behind the abbreviation i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth of March was the date Julius Caesar was assassinated, the warning from the soothsayer.

clue.text: Poem for example written in cathedral city

indicators.note: written in means placed inside, so the abbreviation goes within the city

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: A poem, say, composed in a city with a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small English cathedral city near Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a mournful poem of lament, typically for someone who has died.

clue.text: Cooked fruits crammed with energy in excess

indicators.note: crammed with means stuffed, with something placed inside
cooked signals that the letters of fruits are stewed into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Stewed fruit packed with calories is too much of a good thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges FRUITS, and 'crammed with' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means an overabundance, an amount greater than needed.
